entries.title: II Kings 14:3
segments:
That which was right; externally; in doing, at the commencement of his reign, many things which God had commanded. 
 
External obedience will be followed by temporal benefits; but if it be merely external, it will have no reward hereafter.

entries.title: II Kings 14:7
segments:
The valley of salt; near the south end of the Dead sea. 
 
  Selah; a city of Edom, supposed to be Petra the capital of Edom, situated in a valley surrounded by precipitous rocks in an exceedingly strong position.  Compare

. 
 
  Joktheel; signifying subdued by God.  In going to the war against Edom he had dismissed the large army of Israelites hired to help him, according to God's direction.
In the name now given to Selah, he ascribes his victory over it to God's help.

entries.title: II Kings 14:8
segments: Look one another in the face; engage in battle.  This challenge may have been provoked, in part at least, by the conduct of the Israelitish army which he had dismissed,
.  But it clearly betrayed the pride of his heart in view of his victory over the Edomites, to which he added the sins of idolatry and contempt of God's prophet.
That pride which leads to contention and bloodshed is the fruit of wickedness, the cause of many calamities, and often the forerunner of ruin.

entries.title: II Kings 14:9
segments:
The thistle; representing the kingdom of Judah. 
 
  The cedar; the kingdom of Israel.

entries.title: II Kings 14:14
segments: Hostages; some of the principal men of the city, as security that it would not again molest him.

entries.title: II Kings 14:19
segments: Made a conspiracy against him; thus God, by the hand of wicked men, punished him for his disobedience.  Compare

. 
 
  Lachish; in the south part of Judah.

entries.title: II Kings 14:22
segments:
Elath; at the head of the eastern branch of the Red sea. 
 
  The king; his father Amaziah.

entries.title: II Kings 14:25
segments: Hamath; a city north of Palestine.  See note to

. 
 
  The sea of the plain; the Dead sea, at the south part of the country. 
 
  Gath-hepher; a town in the tribe of Zebulun. 
 
The Lord may govern nations by means of wicked rulers; may enlarge their borders, and thus fulfil his word and accomplish towards his people his own benevolent designs.

entries.title: II Kings 14:28
segments: Damascus, and Hamath; these cities, which were taken from the Syrians in the time of David and Solomon,
, and had been retaken by the Syrians, were now taken from them again by Jeroboam, and restored to Israel.
